name: Yupua
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record jupu1235 (refs, MED, classification Yupua-Siriano-Desano).
Ramirez, Henri. 1997. A Fala Tukano dos Ye'pâ-Masa, Tomo I: Gramática. Manaus: Inspetoria Salesiana (Glottolog cites the 2019 re-edition pp. 5-7 for classification).
sources.note: Mentions †yupúa only in the classification tree (Desanid: Desano + †Yupúa) and historical notes; extinct languages were removed from his comparative lists; nothing on Yupúa accent.
Kobéua wordlists and dance texts; no Yupúa material and no accent remarks found (scanned of tables partly rotated/garbled).

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1914. Betóya-Sprachen Nordwestbrasiliens und der angrenzenden Gebiete (Fortsetzung): Desána, Yupúa, Yahúna, Kueretú. Anthropos 9: 812-832.
sources.note: Comparative wordlist; every Yupúa item carries an acute accent mark (e.g. dólo 'Zunge', póa 'Kopfhaar', múhu 'Hand', dixpelú 'Finger', di(x)kagúu 'Schulter'), with recorded variants such as goxpéga ~ góxpega 'Zahn'. No statement of a rule; raw accent-marked data only.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1913. Betóya-Sprachen Nordwestbrasiliens und der angrenzenden Gebiete [I]. Anthropos 8: 944-977 (Lautlehre pp. 948-949; Bemerkungen zu den einzelnen Sprachen: Yupúa p. 949; earlier Yupúa sources p. 950).
sources.note: Only a transcription key: 'á Wortakzent.' (p. 948) — the acute marks word accent in all vocabularies; diphthongs may carry the acute on the second element. The Yupúa-specific remark (p. 949) concerns fast/indistinct speech, a final verb vowel varying e~u, and a ts/tš/tx cluster — nothing on accent placement.

sources.citation: Martius, C. F. Ph. von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, Bd. II: Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium. Leipzig: Fleischer. Jupuá pp. 275-276; footnote p. 284.
sources.note: Latin-glossed wordlist; nothing on accent (scanned poor but no prose phonology section exists).

sources.citation: Wallace, Alfred R. 1853. A narrative of travels on the Amazon and Rio Negro. London: Reeve. Appendix 'Vocabularies of Amazonian languages', pp. 520ff ('Curetu' list = Yupúa per Koch-Grünberg 1913: 950); Latham's 'Remarks on the vocabularies'.
sources.note: Transcription note only (p. 521): 'the accent shows where the stress is to be laid'; adds that 'Curetu and Tucano are particularly harsh and guttural'. No placement rule.

sources.citation: Chacon, Thiago. 2014. A revised proposal of Proto-Tukanoan consonants and Tukanoan family classification. International Journal of American Linguistics 80(3): 275-322.
